name: PULSE
tagline: Incident response from 20 minutes to 10 seconds

starry.situation: A North America-based service provider supported 90 clients across finance and commerce. Clients were frustrated: ticket response times averaged over 20 minutes, creating significant dissatisfaction and reputational risk.
starry.task: The challenge was to reduce response times drastically, implement improvements at scale for all clients, maintain the existing toolset, and work within the constraints of current staffing levels.
starry.action:
We conducted a structured discovery and designed an event processing pipeline. By analyzing each step (issue recognition, response, and ticket creation), we identified latency gaps. We then:
  • Instrumented and timestamped all actions
  • Centralized tooling to simplify workflows
  • Automated ticket creation via the pipeline
  • Implemented duplicate suppression and client notification triggers
starry.result: Response time dropped from 20 minutes to 10 seconds, a 99.17% improvement. The solution scaled across all clients and proved durable under data load.
starry.reflection: Engaging operations early helped align the platform with how the team worked and delivered business services. Involving people across the process flow avoided development in isolation and mismatches at handoff. Their feedback informed improvements and enhancements to the platform.
starry.yield: By automating routine L1 operations, including ticket creation, information distribution, and meeting coordination, the platform released an estimated $2.2 million in annual operational capacity, based on 35 people working 1,800 hours annually at $35 per hour. The team could redirect that capacity toward existing clients without additional staffing. This represents capacity released, rather than payroll savings. Remediation remained with a separate L2 team. Extend your reach: give the existing team the capacity to accomplish more.
